sentences.text:
The following arguments made by Sri Manish Kumar Kashyap, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The delay of 8 days in lodgment of the FIR in the facts and circumstances of the case is fatal to the prosecution case.
2. The FIR arises out of a financial dispute.
3. The victim and her husband were in employ of the applicant and his brother.
They worked as labourers.
4. There was a financial dispute between the parties.
5. The applicant has been falsely nominated by the victim to avoid paying her dues.
6. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents to save the failing prosecution case.
7. It is noteworthy that the victim in her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she travelled from Delhi to Badaun.
Thereafter, she accompanied the applicant in a vehicle to Kasganj.
8. Prosecution case that the applicant's elder brother was standing as guard while the applicant was committing rape with the victim is inherently improbable and liable to be disbelieved.
9. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.

10. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C.
and Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
11. Medical evidence to establish the commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.

In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Sanjay be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
